summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and volume overload. He was found to have acute on chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, acute kidney injury secondary to cardiorenal syndrome, and concomitant pneumonia. He required ICU-level care for hypoxic respiratory failure and transient encephalopathy, managed with BiPAP, aggressive diuresis, and antibiotics. His renal function improved with treatment, and he was transitioned from IV to oral diuretics. His atrial fibrillation was rate-controlled with increased carvedilol, and his anticoagulation was optimized. He stabilized, regained baseline mental status, and was discharged home on increased torsemide, adjusted immunosuppression, and a revised insulin regimen with close outpatient follow-up.
